title: Epochal replay harness & frame-level VCR runner for cross-SDK streaming contracts
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Goal: build a replay harness that records and deterministically replays streaming interactions (responses and per-frame events) across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. This ticket implements a 'frame-level VCR' format and a runner called the Epochal Replay Harness (ERH) which lets SDK tests: 1) capture live traffic from Redwood's staging API with controlled timestamp normalization; 2) scrub sensitive fields and canonicalize non-deterministic tokens; 3) produce compact epochal recordings (frames + metadata + checksum); 4) replay at test-time with programmable latency, connection drops, and backpressure to validate retry and streaming ergonomics; 5) assert contract invariants (HTTP shape, chunk framing order, event types, final token checksums) and output a human-readable diff for CI failures.

Why this is needed: existing VCR-style fixtures handle request/response but not continuous streaming frames, partial sends, or KV-cache warmup patterns. Several flakies in streaming SDKs are caused by frame boundary differences, intermittent backpressure, and race-y retry behavior. A recording that captures per-frame timing plus an ability to mutate timing during replay will surface regressions cross-language.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Recording format: JSONL with base64-encoded frame payloads + epoch metadata + a deterministic checksum. Chosen for inspectability and cross-platform decoding. Binary pack formats considered (CBOR) but deferred due to debuggability and toolchain friction.
- Transport emulation: implement at HTTP/2 frame layer for our Node/Python SDKs and fallback to chunk-level emulation for Go where lower-level hooks are harder to instrument. This compromises perfect parity for Go but keeps coverage high.
- Time normalization: recordings include both wall-clock and logical timestamps. The ERH will support 'timewarp' presets (fast-forward OR controlled jitter) to accelerate CI and reproduce latency-sensitive bugs.
- Failure injection: offer named presets (drop-1-in-n, tail-latency-spike, early-reset) to run deterministic stress cases. Avoid fuzzing in CI default runs to preserve determinism.

Implementation plan:
1) Recorder shim in staging proxy (safelist customer IDs) that emits epochal JSONL files and uploads to S3/fixture store. (ENG-41207 is the proxy work that provides hooks.)
2) Local runner library in each SDK repo (python/ts/go) that can: load recording, provide a mockserver endpoint, apply timewarp and failure presets, and expose assertion helpers. Priority: Python & TypeScript first.
3) Contract assertion layer: canonical tokenization step + frame-order invariants + optional golden checksum comparison. Add CLI tool `erh-assert` that emits structured test results for CI.
4) CI integration: a small set of canonical recordings will be gated in PR checks for streaming-related changes. Non-blocking but required for release branches.

Acceptance criteria:
- Recorder in staging can produce an epochal JSONL file for a streaming chat session containing at least: request headers, per-frame payloads, frame timestamps, and top-level checksum.
- Python and TypeScript SDK runners can replay a recording deterministically (no flakiness in 30 repeated runs) under default preset.
- Runner supports at least 3 failure-presets and 'timewarp' mode.
- `erh-assert` produces clear diffs-aid with links to artifact on failure and is integrated into CI for the SDK monorepo.

Backward compatibility & migration: existing fixtures (VCR) will be migrated by a small conversion tool. Older non-streaming tests remain untouched.

Observability & metrics: runner emits a small JSON result with keys: run_id, fixture_id, preset, frame_count, mismatch_count, runtime_ms which will be uploaded to our test-dashboard to correlate flakiness.

Risks: potential data leakage from recordings (mitigated via scrubbing pipeline and upload ACLs), and increased CI runtime (mitigated with timewarp acceleration).

Next steps: implement recorder shim + schema, ship python runner POC, circulate design doc to SDK owners, and land CI gate for streaming smoke tests.
